# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Six fabs near Dallas are under discussion as TSMC's second U.S. hub.**

**What You Need to Know:** Reported plans put six advanced wafer fabs near Dallas on the table as TSMC's second U.S. chip hub after Arizona. Chosunbiz, citing Taiwan's United Daily News and Economic Daily News, says TSMC has not officially announced the complex, while some analyses put the spend above the $265 billion planned for Arizona. The capacity, if it is built, is framed as sitting close to Nvidia, AMD and Apple.

### Top Story
Chosunbiz reports that equipment makers, via Taiwan's United Daily News and Economic Daily News, expect TSMC to be reviewing the Dallas area as a second U.S. advanced-chip complex after Arizona, aimed at AI-chip demand and at customers including Nvidia, AMD and Apple. Six advanced wafer plants are being discussed, and TSMC has not officially announced the plans. Some analyses say the investment could surpass the $265 billion, about 360 trillion won, planned for the Arizona base, and some expect a finer process than the one applied in Arizona. Phoenix is already being built out with wafer fabs plus advanced packaging and R&D so AI and high-performance computing chips can be produced locally. If Texas went ahead, TSMC would have two large southern U.S. hubs; there is also word of shaping that pair into a "southern semiconductor dual-core corridor," in a region already called Silicon Prairie, where Texas Instruments and Samsung are investing in large semiconductor plants. The packaging-plant additions reported yesterday were in Taiwan; this item is a reported U.S. wafer complex, not an announced fab. Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-it/2026/09/29/VLJD5FS2PFAS7GW2CIYKXYJLBA/)

### Silicon
**Arm Unveils Neoverse CSS N4 for Agentic AI Silicon:** Arm
Arm says Neoverse CSS N4 is designed to give partners more flexibility, more customization and a faster path to differentiated silicon for the agentic AI era. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2104735527148642376)

**AMD Announces Acquisition of World Labs:** AMD
AMD says it has a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, bringing researchers and model experts who will help shape future AI infrastructure and strengthen the open AI ecosystem. AMD named Fei-Fei Li and the World Labs team. World Labs said it is joining AMD and that its work since its founding in 2024 has set a vision for AI applied to the spatial and physical world. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2104665475263115678)

**Samsung's 2nm Yield Approaches 60%, Leveraging Tesla Orders to Challenge TSMC:** BigGo
BigGo reports Samsung's 2nm yield approaching 60 percent, with Tesla orders used to challenge TSMC. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/fbe9fae2-30b9-45e1-ba81-d206c28da6b8)

### Data Centres & Power
**The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy:** Data Center Knowledge
Data Center Knowledge reports global data-centre power demand projected to exceed 200 gigawatts by 2030, with individual campuses scaling into the hundreds of megawatts and beyond. At Data Center World Power in Dallas, held September 21–23, Scott Hart, executive vice president of NRG Business, said data centres were traditionally grid-connected 20- to 40-megawatt facilities, cloud campuses then reached about 100 megawatts, and conversations have now pivoted to a gigawatt and beyond. Hart said a project of that scale makes it hard for a utility to commit to building a power plant, because a technology clock runs in months or a few years while power infrastructure runs in decades, and utilities plan and finance assets over 15–30 years. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/the-200-gw-moment-reinventing-the-grid-for-the-ai-economy)

**Investing for a high performance future:** Data Center Dynamics
Data Center Dynamics is carrying a white paper on how waterless two-phase liquid cooling can support high-density compute and sustained performance in low-latency trading environments. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/whitepapers/investing-for-a-high-performance-future-2026/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Intel Cites a €5 Billion Leixlip Expansion Beside Long Arizona Manufacturing:** Intel
Intel, in a public reply, cites a presence of more than 30 years in Leixlip and a recent €5 billion expansion there, alongside more than 40 years of manufacturing in Arizona. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/intel/status/2104656237749039135)

**TSMC is raising 3nm chip prices up to 15% and nobody can say no:** Startup Fortune
Startup Fortune reports TSMC raising 3-nanometer chip prices by up to 15 percent. Source: [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/tsmc-is-raising-3nm-chip-prices-up-to-15-and-nobody-can-say-no/)

**Beyond 16 layers: HBM stacks test advanced packaging equipment makers:** Digitimes
Digitimes reports that HBM stacks beyond 16 layers are testing advanced packaging equipment makers. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260929PD221/packaging-equipment-hbm-2026-materials.html)

### The Teardown: When the Rack's Coolant Has to Change
Heat leaves the rack, or the accelerators throttle. Data Center Knowledge, citing Bill Kleyman, reports AI workloads driving typical rack densities from roughly 10–30 kilowatts into 80–150 kilowatts, with advanced deployments approaching 1 megawatt per rack.

Air cooling is a volume problem. Fans push room air across a heatsink; the air carries heat to a coil elsewhere in the building. The ceiling is flow. More flow means more pressure drop through the cabinet, more risk that hot-aisle air comes back to the inlet, and a point where the electrical feed and the airflow fail together. Another card in that rack then adds temperature, not useful work.

Liquid cooling changes the carrier, not the need to reject the heat. A pump moves water or a dielectric across a cold plate, or the board sits in a bath, and a coolant distribution unit hands the load to the building loop. A small liquid flow moves heat that would have required a large air flow. Kleyman tied that shift to AFCOM's State of the Data Center 2026 survey: 69 percent of respondents expect rack density to increase like nothing seen in the past, and liquid-cooling adoption is showing 36 percent growth.

The parts in the rack show why the old air budget breaks. Kleyman said a standard rack can hold six Nvidia DGX-class systems, each built around eight H100 accelerators, with individual accelerator cards costing up to $40,000. That population does not fit a 10–30 kilowatt cabinet as a full set. It starts to fit between 80 and 150 kilowatts. Near 1 megawatt per rack, the design is busbar plus coolant loop, not a deeper air plenum.

The tradeoff flips inside the old 10–30 kilowatt band. Pumps and plates then add leak paths without buying accelerators the air system could already feed. Once a deployment approaches 1 megawatt per rack, staying on air means leaving some of those $40,000 cards out, or asking the hall for airflow it cannot move.

### On the Horizon
- September 30: CoreWeave's Pioneer's Night runs 5–7pm at Moscone South, with an AMA by its CTO and co-founder, ahead of #FullyConnected26 keynotes.
- September 30: Framework opens pre-orders for the Desktop with the Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495; the motherboard and case stay the same for backwards compatibility, and the high-end configuration tops out at 192 GB of LPDDR5X-8533, against 128 GB on the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 version.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **VisionPower Semiconductor opens its first 300 mm fab in Singapore and enters risk production with volume output due in the first quarter of 2027.**

**What You Need to Know:** VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company opened its first 300 mm fab in Tampines, Singapore. The facility supports 130 nm to 40 nm processes for mixed-signal, power management, analog and interposer applications. Volume production begins in the first quarter of 2027. The company is a joint venture between Vanguard International Semiconductor Corporation and NXP Semiconductors. Construction finished after 22 months. The first sample lot achieved yields above 99 percent. Singapore's Minister for Trade and Industry attended the opening along with the Chairman of the Singapore Economic Development Board and the Chief Executive Officer of JTC Corporation.

### Top Story
The facility has completed construction. The fab has entered risk production. The fab supports process technologies from 130 nm to 40 nm. These processes cover mixed-signal applications. They also cover power management. Analog applications are included. Interposer applications are supported. The end markets include high-performance computing. Mobile markets are served. Automotive markets are served. Industrial markets are served. Consumer markets are served. The opening ceremony included Singapore's Minister for Trade and Industry. The Chairman of the Singapore Economic Development Board attended. The Chief Executive Officer of JTC Corporation attended. The joint venture was established in September 2024. A groundbreaking ceremony took place in December of the same year. The fab processed its first sample lot successfully. Representatives from TSMC and other partners were present at the event. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353149/vsmc-celebrates-the-grand-opening-of-its-first-300-mm-fab-in-singapore)

### Silicon
**SK hynix validates HBM5 with TSMC on CoWoS:** South Korea's SK hynix has been named Partner of the Year for the second consecutive year by TSMC. The award falls in the 3D Fabric-HBM Integration category. The recognition stems from joint validation of HBM5 high-bandwidth memory. Validation occurred on TSMC's CoWoS 2.5D advanced packaging technology. HBM5 sits three generations ahead of the HBM3E now used in AI servers. SK hynix began shipping HBM4 in the second quarter of this year. The company is supplying samples of HBM4E to key customers. HBM5 remains in the validation stage. The portfolio on display at the TSMC Open Innovation Platform conference spanned HBM4 to server DRAM and enterprise SSDs. SK hynix showed a 12-high 36-gigabyte HBM4 module. A 96-gigabyte SOCAMM2 module was also shown. These components target Nvidia's Vera Rubin superchip. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/36a62c2a-97bc-440c-805a-2cf40456dd41)

**Xcena MX1 combines DDR5, SSDs and RISC-V cores over CXL:** Xcena’s MX1 uses CXL to push compute into memory. The design combines DDR5, SSDs and RISC-V cores. Data movement is reduced to address memory bottlenecks in AI workloads. Programmability is eased by the architecture. The RISC-V cores sit directly alongside the memory arrays. Local reductions and filtering occur before data crosses the host PCIe bus. Each CXL-attached module therefore cuts traffic volume. The SSDs serve as a slower but larger tier. The RISC-V cores can address this tier without first staging everything in host DRAM. Latency stays comparable to local memory when the working set fits inside the pooled DDR5. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/xcena-cuts-data-movement-to-address-memory-bottlenecks/)

**INNO3D launches AWS-511Z-R1 workstation with up to four Blackwell GPUs:** INNO3D announced the AWS-511Z-R1 Tower Workstation. The system is powered by Intel Xeon W-3400 processors. It supports up to 2 TB DDR5 memory. The workstation supports up to four NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Workstation Edition GPUs. It also supports two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition GPUs. Target workloads include AI development, engineering simulation, digital twins, 3D content creation and data-intensive tasks. The platform brings AI and accelerated computing closer to businesses and professionals. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353146/inno3d-launches-the-tower-workstation-aws-511z-r1)

### Data Centres & Power
**A*STAR advanced packaging lab draws 50 companies and S$46 million:** A*STAR's advanced packaging lab has drawn 50 companies. Investment totals S$46 million. Applied Materials is expanding the lab. The expansion supports further collaboration on advanced packaging technologies. Source: [crnasia.com](https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/components-and-peripherals/astar-s-advanced-packaging-lab-has-drawn-50-companies-and-s)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**TSMC 2 nm wafer capacity to exceed earlier estimates:** TSMC 2 nm wafer capacity is expected to exceed earlier estimates. The update comes from EDN reports. Capacity growth addresses surging demand for advanced AI chips. Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/tsmc-2nm-wafer-capacity-exceed-030730906.html)

**Synopsys and TSMC expand collaboration for next-generation AI system design:** Synopsys and TSMC have expanded their collaboration. The expanded work supports next-generation AI system design. The partnership focuses on tools and flows for advanced nodes and packaging. Source: [newelectronics.co.uk](https://www.newelectronics.co.uk/content/news/synopsys-and-tsmc-expand-collaboration-to-support-next-generation-ai-system-design)

### The Teardown: CXL Memory Pooling in the MX1
Take it apart and the MX1 places RISC-V cores directly alongside DDR5 and SSD arrays connected through CXL links. This layout lets the cores perform local reductions and filtering before any data crosses the host PCIe bus. Each CXL-attached module therefore cuts the volume of traffic that would otherwise traverse the narrower host interface. The design also lets the SSDs serve as a slower but larger tier that the RISC-V cores can address without first staging everything in host DRAM. When the working set fits inside the pooled DDR5, latency stays comparable to local memory; once the set spills to the SSD tier, bandwidth drops but capacity scales without adding more host sockets. The tradeoff flips when the ratio of compute to data movement exceeds the CXL link rate, at which point the added cores no longer offset the extra hop.

### On the Horizon
- Volume production at the new VisionPower Semiconductor 300 mm fab in Singapore begins in the first quarter of 2027.
- SK hynix is already shipping HBM4 samples of HBM4E to key customers while HBM5 validation continues on TSMC CoWoS.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **One hundred fifty billion dollars, reported for Solidigm, would bankroll SK hynix memory expansion.**

**What You Need to Know:** SK hynix is discussing a Solidigm listing at up to $150 billion, a raise that would fund memory expansion, and the company has not confirmed it. Second-quarter operating profit was 60.5426 trillion won on revenue of 79.3187 trillion won, with Counterpoint putting HBM share at 50 percent. Separately, AMD restated a Helios rack claim of 31 TB of HBM4, and summit readouts left US chip controls unmentioned.

### Top Story
AD HOC NEWS, citing a Reuters report, says SK hynix held preliminary talks with investment banks on Friday about a multibillion-dollar IPO of US NAND subsidiary Solidigm. A valuation of up to $150 billion and a capital raise of roughly $15 billion are under discussion. The company has not officially confirmed the listing plans. In the second quarter it posted operating profit of 60.5426 trillion won on revenue of 79.3187 trillion won. Counterpoint said SK hynix held a 50 percent share of the global HBM market in that period. Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/sk-hynix-s-bonus-fueled-boom-parental-leave-drops-as-solidigm-ipo-talk/70188830)

### Silicon
**Helios Rack Claim Lists 31 TB of HBM4: AMD**
AMD said Helios delivers over 18,000 CDNA 5 GPU compute units in a single rack. The same claim lists 4,600 Zen 6 CPU cores. Memory in the claim is 31 TB of HBM4. The post looks back at Advancing AI with Dr. Lisa Su, so this is a restatement of that event's rack claim, not a shipment notice. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2103854831899140287)

**Qualcomm Announces Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome reports Qualcomm announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 at its Snapdragon Summit. New Oryon CPU cores reach 5 GHz for the first time. The parts add GPU matrix cores and LPDDR6, plus new Wi-Fi and cellular radios. Extreme is the fastest, most feature-rich SKU; the other Gen 6 chip has fewer features, a split by features rather than the Gen 5 V-series approach of a smaller GPU. The comparison lists 5G Advanced downlink at 12.5 Gbps on one configuration and 14.8 Gbps on the others, both with dual active SIM. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/qualcomm-unveils-snapdragon-8-elite-gen-6-and-elite-extreme-gen-6-next-gen-flagship-mobile-chips/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Russia Targets Ukrainian Data Centers: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware reports Russia has begun targeting data centers and internet infrastructure in Ukraine. The attacks left 100,000 households in the area without an internet connection. A senior government official said the country's internet network is highly decentralized. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/russia-bombs-ukrainian-data-centers-in-latest-escalation-100-000-households-lose-connectivity-as-firms-migrate-data-abroad-zelensky-says-ordinary-life-is-simply-a-target)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Xi-Trump Summit Left Chip Controls Off the Readout: UA.NEWS**
UA.NEWS, citing the South China Morning Post, reports US chip export controls were not a main topic at the Xi-Trump summit in Washington, and final statements from Beijing and Washington contain no direct mention of the restrictions. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC that export-control issues related to national security were not considered as part of this week's trade negotiations. The administration has largely retained the October 2022 rules, so the quiet readout is not a lifting of the controls. A Taipei-based research company forecasts the share of Nvidia, AMD and other foreign suppliers will decline to 21 percent in 2026 from 34 percent last year. Nvidia wrote off $400 million in the first half on excess H200 inventory caused by approval delays. Paul Triolo of DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group warned the pause may be temporary and pointed to the Match Act, meant to push Japan and the Netherlands to coordinate limits on sales of advanced chipmaking equipment to China. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/eksportnii-kontrol-ssha-nad-chipami-ne-stav-kliuchovoiu-temoiu-samitu-si-i-trampa-south-china-morning-post)

**Guai Guai Strike Vote Follows ASE Site Purchase: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware, citing the Taipei Times, reports 94 percent of workers at Guai Guai's Zhongli factory voted for strike action after the company said it would relocate to Hsinchu. Workers were offered a 5 percent pay increase, which the union says merely tracks Taiwan's newly announced minimum-wage change. ASE bought the Zhongli site for NT$5.6 billion, or US$176.1 million, and the union says no share of that sum goes to workers. The union wants written severance guarantees and, for those who stay, a NT$10,000, or US$315, monthly increase. Workers are waiting on the company's response. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/taiwans-chip-talisman-snack-faces-production-halt-after-94-percent-strike-vote-workers-demand-share-of-usd176-million-factory-sale-to-ase)

### The Teardown: Qualifying a Packaging Tool Beside the Vendor
An advanced packaging tool is not qualified when it is unpacked. It is qualified when bond alignment, bond force, and the heat steps around a logic die and a memory stack have been run on the customer's flow, with the customer's limits deciding pass or fail. A vendor's own demonstration line cannot finish that job, because the warpage, the stack, and the test limits belong to the customer. That is why a verification center is built as a shared floor, not as another brochure lab.

Taiwan Economic Daily News, reported by Asiae, says the groundbreaking for the Kaohsiung Baifu Industrial Park was held on September 21. TSMC, the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the Kaohsiung city government are starting what the report calls Taiwan's first advanced semiconductor equipment and materials verification center. The plan puts TSMC's advanced packaging verification center, a talent development center, and exclusive factories for partner companies on one site. Asiae reports that more than 20 suppliers are already planning to move in, and that TSMC is committed to supporting that move-in.

The mechanism is proximity. A process tweak on a bonder can be tried, measured, and rejected beside the customer's verification team, instead of being discovered after the tool has been dropped into a hall that is already running volume. Scrap at that stage is not a blank wafer. It is a finished die joined to finished memory. Keeping the tool company and the packaging customer on one site is how that scrap is supposed to stay off the volume line.

Asiae says a standard factory is scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2028, and that the verification laboratory and the talent development center are set to open in phases in the fourth quarter of the same year. The tradeoff flips if that shared lab arrives later than a tool slot on a line that already exists. Partners who cannot wait until 2028 will still qualify across separate sites. The September 21 groundbreaking starts construction of the loop.

### On the Horizon
- A Solidigm listing could come as early as 2027, AD HOC NEWS reports from Reuters, and SK hynix has not officially confirmed it.
- Starting in the first quarter of next year, companies are to begin leasing land and building at Kaohsiung Baifu, with third-party testing and inspection services in the second quarter, Asiae reports.
- ServeTheHome says the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 parts set Qualcomm's high-end mobile offerings for next year.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Forty-four billion dollars approved still leaves TSMC's Arizona plan at two hundred sixty-five billion.**

**What You Need to Know:** Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs has approved forty-four billion dollars of TSMC U.S. investment since December 2020, against a two hundred sixty-five billion dollar Arizona plan. Intel is telling a KeyBanc audience that 14A should land within 5 percent of TSMC's A14, with risk production in the second half of 2027. HANMI has shipped its first FC Bonder 75 for 2.5D system-semiconductor packaging.

### Top Story
Focus Taiwan reports that Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs has approved TSMC applications to invest US$44 billion in the United States since December 2020, while the chipmaker pursues a US$265 billion investment plan in Arizona. The ministry's Department of Investment Review has cleared seven applications: US$30.001 million in December 2020 to establish TSMC Arizona, then US$3.47 billion that same month, US$3.5 billion in March 2023, US$4.5 billion in September 2023, US$5.0 billion in June 2024, US$7.5 billion in September 2024, and US$20 billion in July, each to raise capital in the Arizona subsidiary. In March 2025 TSMC announced an additional US$100 billion on top of US$65 billion previously announced, to take advanced wafer fabs in Arizona from three to six and to build two advanced IC assembly plants and a research and development center. At a mid-July investor conference, chairman C.C. Wei said that additional US$100 billion would build four more wafer fabs and expand IC packaging capacity. In July the company raised its 2026 capital-expenditure forecast to US$60 billion–US$64 billion, from US$52 billion–US$56 billion set out in mid-April, and the ministry expects further approval filings at this pace. TSMC operates 19 advanced wafer fabs and IC assembly plants in Taiwan and is building 13 more fabs and packaging facilities in Hsinchu, Taichung, Chiayi, Tainan and Kaohsiung; the ministry's stated priorities are that the largest capacity, the most advanced technologies, and the most complete ecosystem stay in Taiwan. Source: [focustaiwan.tw](https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202609260007)

### Silicon
**Intel Expects 14A Node to Be Within 5% of TSMC's A14:** TechPowerUp
TechPowerUp reports that Intel Foundry chief Naga Chandrasekaran told KeyBanc Capital Markets Intel expects its 14A node to land within 5 percent of TSMC's A14, without saying whether that gap is performance, power, density, an advantage, a disadvantage, or a mix. Intel 18A is the node that is shipping. 14A risk production is planned for the second half of 2027, with high-volume production expected in 2028, after tens of thousands of 14A pilot wafers and further yield work plus minor node adjustments before risk production next year. Against Intel 18A, 14A is described as a 15 to 20 percent performance gain at the same power, or a 25 to 35 percent power cut at the same performance, with up to a 30 percent density gain, and the report does not say whether that density figure is logic or SRAM. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353094/intel-expects-14a-node-to-be-within-5-of-tsmcs-a14)

**HANMI Semiconductor Ships First FC Bonder 75 for AI System Semiconductors:** Semiconductor Digest
HANMI Semiconductor has shipped the first FC Bonder 75 to a customer. The tool is designed for 2.5D AI semiconductor packaging and is the company's move beyond high-bandwidth memory into system-semiconductor packaging. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/hanmi-semiconductor-ships-first-fc-bonder-75-for-ai-system-semiconductors/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=hanmi-semiconductor-ships-first-fc-bonder-75-for-ai-system-semiconductors)

**Huawei and Alibaba Tout Progress in AI Chip, Clusters, and Models:** HPCwire
HPCwire reports that at Huawei Connect 2026 in Shanghai on September 17, Huawei showed new cluster, interconnect, and storage offerings. Alibaba showed new chips and servers at the same push on scale. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/09/25/huawei-and-alibaba-tout-progress-in-ai-chip-clusters-and-models/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Vocus to build 4,000km fiber link between Brisbane and Darwin:** Data Center Dynamics
Vocus is set to build a 4,000-kilometre fibre route between Brisbane and Darwin. Data Center Dynamics reports the route is aimed at demand from hyperscaler, neocloud, and enterprise customers. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/vocus-to-build-4000km-fiber-link-between-brisbane-and-darwin/)

**Google’s Grid-Interactive AI Data Centers: From Backup to Grid Partner:** Data Center Knowledge
At Data Center World Power, Google's Tom Garvens described full-stack design, low-voltage direct current power, battery energy storage, and liquid cooling as the stack Google is using so hyperscale AI sites can act as grid partners rather than only as backup load. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/google-s-grid-interactive-ai-data-centers-from-backup-to-grid-partner)

**Efforts to Curb Data Center Speculation Gain Ground Across the US:** Data Center Knowledge
Large-load tariffs and other screens meant to weed out speculative data-centre projects are taking shape. Data Center Knowledge ties that shift to public backlash against data centres and to changing state-level policy. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/efforts-to-curb-data-center-speculation-gain-ground-across-the-us)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**TSMC foundry market share: 72.5% in Q2 2026:** NeoTeo
NeoTeo reports TSMC held an estimated 72.5 percent of foundry revenue in the second quarter of 2026. Source: [neoteo.com](https://www.neoteo.com/en/tsmc-held-an-estimated-725-of-foundry-revenue-in-q2-2026)

**Singapore Announces SG Semiconductor:** Semiconductor Digest
Singapore has unveiled SG Semiconductor, a national identity for its semiconductor sector. Semiconductor Digest says the point is to raise global visibility and to connect companies with the country's ecosystem and talent. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/singapore-announces-sg-semiconductor/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=singapore-announces-sg-semiconductor)

### The Teardown: The Row CDU Still Sets the Hall
An in-row coolant distribution unit takes heat off a secondary loop at the end of the aisle, so the cold plate on the package is not the building heat exchanger. StorageReview reports Supermicro NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks now shipping with 1.8-megawatt in-row CDUs and a 1,152-GPU scalable unit. That 1.8 megawatts is the thermal duty the row exchanger is built to move continuously. The 1,152-GPU count is the failure domain: pumps, valves, manifolds, and power for that many accelerators sit behind one scalable-unit boundary, so a flow fault is a row event. A CDU at that rating is plant equipment. Quick-disconnects, heat exchangers, and redundant pumps have to be qualified as a mechanical system before the hall accepts the IT load. AMD, in a separate validation note, describes a double-wide rack at 8,000 pounds lifted onto a vibration test while Helios is checked for real-world handling. Liquid manifolds and a chassis that wide add mass; the shaker is how joints and connectors are shown to survive lift and floor vibration before coolant is trusted in the row. Pluang reports, which is the demand pulling these row designs into shipping racks rather than lab slides. Chip-level efficiency does not retire the row plant by itself. The tradeoff flips only when the GPU count inside the scalable unit drops, or when heat per GPU falls far enough that a smaller CDU can cover the same row. Until one of those two moves, pipes, pumps, and floor loading are sized to the 1.8-megawatt row and the 8,000-pound lift.

### On the Horizon
- CoreWeave's Fully Connected 2026 conference is next week.
- ServeTheHome frames AMD's EPYC 9006 Venice, with Zen 6 coming to servers, as a launch that is approaching, and sets the window for what to expect from the company between now and late 2027.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Applied Digital's $3.2 billion plan places 210 megawatts near Brookwood, Alabama.**

**What You Need to Know:** Applied Digital's $3.2 billion plan places 210 megawatts near Brookwood, Alabama. The campus is Delta Forge 2, with operations expected in 2028 on a 1,300-acre site. Vertiv is also buying Irish fluid-management firm King Environmental Services to extend liquid-cooling field work into EMEA.

### Top Story
Applied Digital has announced a 210-megawatt AI data center, Delta Forge 2, near Brookwood in Alabama’s Tuscaloosa County, and puts the project at $3.2 billion. The campus sits on 1,300 acres and spans 1.2 million square feet at full build-out, with operations expected to begin in 2028. It is set to support up to 1,000 construction jobs and 100 permanent roles. Applied Digital describes the customer as an investment-grade hyperscaler; in June it had said that customer was secured for a 210-megawatt center without naming this site. The company is committing $270 million in community benefits to the Tuscaloosa County Economic Development Authority over 20 years, alongside an estimated $131 million in tax revenue. Its contracted portfolio now spans five AI Factory campuses, totaling 1.4 gigawatts of critical IT load and approximately 2.15 gigawatts of grid-connected utility power. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/applied-digital-reveals-32bn-delta-forge-2-ai-data-center-will-be-built-in-alabama/)

### Silicon
**Micron SVP says agentic AI runs on two compute stacks: Micron Technology**
Micron’s Jeremy Werner, senior vice president and general manager of the Core Data Center Business Unit, says agentic AI runs on two compute stacks rather than one. The GPU reasons and plans, while the CPU orchestrates actions. KV cache is the technology he points to for keeping context available. He says growing context sizes and agentic workloads are driving memory needs far beyond reasoning alone. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/MicronTech/status/2103279887410921630)

**ASRock Rack reviews a new EPYC 8005 Sorano board: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome has published a review of the ASRock Rack SORANOD8-2L2T, a new motherboard for the AMD EPYC 8005 “Sorano” series. The board is described as providing lots of connectivity for that processor family. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/asrock-rack-soranod8-2l2t-review-a-new-amd-epyc-8005-sorano-motherboard/)

**Fraunhofer IAF builds a broadband amplifier for data-centre links: Semiconductor Digest**
Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Solid State Physics IAF have developed a monolithic microwave integrated circuit for modern data centers, measurement systems and sensors. Semiconductor Digest describes the part as a broadband distributed amplifier with outstanding performance. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/broadband-distributed-amplifier-for-data-centers-measurement-systems-and-sensors/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=broadband-distributed-amplifier-for-data-centers-measurement-systems-and-sensors)

### Data Centres & Power
**Vertiv agrees to buy King Environmental Services: Data Center Dynamics**
Vertiv has agreed to acquire Ireland-based King Environmental Services, which provides fluid management, commissioning and load-testing for high-density, liquid-cooled data centers. The deal is meant to extend Vertiv’s thermal-management services into EMEA; the company already offers fluid management in North America. Last year Vertiv bought PurgeRite, another firm in the same work, for more than $1 billion. Chief executive Gio Albertazzi said that as computing density increases, cooling and power performance “will depend as much on execution in the field as on engineering and system design.” KES, founded in 2002 and headquartered near Dublin, serves customers across EMEA, and its site lists projects for Microsoft and Equinix. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/vertiv-to-acquire-data-center-fluid-management-firm-king-environmental-services/)

**Communities scrutinize data-centre infrasound: Data Center Knowledge**
Data Center Knowledge reports that infrasound produced by data centers is increasingly scrutinized by communities. The piece argues that proactive mitigation and transparent communication are essential for operators. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/low-frequency-noise-and-data-centers-what-to-know)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**ACCM adds US laminate and prepreg capacity in Wisconsin: Semiconductor Digest**
ACCM is expanding US manufacturing capacity across four advanced materials segments for AI infrastructure at its Wisconsin facility. Laminate capacity of 20 million square feet per year is scheduled online in January 2027. Build-up and prepreg capacity of 87 million square feet per year is scheduled online in November 2026. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/accm-expands-us-manufacturing-capacity-across-four-advanced-materials-segments-for-ai-infrastructure/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=accm-expands-us-manufacturing-capacity-across-four-advanced-materials-segments-for-ai-infrastructure)

**Chip supply chains tighten for equipment and materials: Semiconductor Engineering**
Semiconductor Engineering’s week in review reports that chip supply chains are tightening for equipment and critical materials. It also reports that TSMC partners are accelerating, and that China is doubling down on AI compute and memory. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-157/)

### The Teardown: Rack Mass Versus Rack Price
You take it apart at the floor plate, not at the silicon. A data-centre slab is rated for a point load and a uniform load, and the rack designer spends that allowance on busbar, manifold, cold plates and coolant until the frame is as heavy as the tile allows. The invoice is not part of that drawing. Dylan Patel wrote that a fully populated GB300 NVL72 weighs roughly 1,580 kilograms, that recent purchase orders put the rack at 5 million dollars, that the GB200 NVL72 was 4 million dollars, and that Vera Rubin NVL72 is already quoted at up to 8.8 million dollars at essentially the same rack mass. Those four figures sit on one chassis envelope. High-bandwidth memory, the CoWoS package that bonds it to the GPU, and the power stages that feed both add little mass and most of the price. Patel's point is that those three stay supply-limited, so dollars per kilogram rise while floor loading holds the kilogram count still. The unit you accept on the dock is the populated rack, which is why he prices the frame rather than the bare packages. A higher quote does not buy a heavier rack, and a heavier rack would not clear a slab already at its rating. The tradeoff flips when packaging allocation or feeder capacity, not steel, is what you lack: price can move inside a fixed tile, and the tile cannot grow to match the quote.

### On the Horizon
- Vertiv expects the King Environmental Services acquisition to close before the end of 2026.
- Applied Digital anticipates initial operations in August 2027 at Polaris Forge 3, a 300-megawatt critical IT load on 600 acres in an unnamed northern state, for the same US investment-grade hyperscaler previously signed for Delta Forge 1.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Three ClusterMAX reports leave only CoreWeave platinum for AI cluster operations.**

**What You Need to Know:** SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 3.0 leaves CoreWeave the only provider rated platinum across three editions. Dylan Patel, founder of SemiAnalysis, called CoreWeave the operational benchmark for the industry. The rating is an operations score for GPU cloud clusters, not a new chip shipment.

### Top Story
CoreWeave said SemiAnalysis published ClusterMAX 3.0 and that CoreWeave is the only provider rated Platinum in all three editions. Dylan Patel, founder of SemiAnalysis, is quoted by CoreWeave: "CoreWeave remains the operational benchmark for the industry." CoreWeave posted that line on September 23, 2026, with the rating presented as an operations benchmark for the industry, not as a parts launch. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2102874377284890921)

### Silicon
**CXMT gains ground in DRAM as Samsung and SK Hynix shift capacity to HBM: Digitimes**
Digitimes reports CXMT is gaining ground in DRAM. The same report ties that shift to Samsung and SK Hynix moving more capacity toward HBM. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260924VL219/dram-cxmt-samsung-hbm-capacity.html)

**Aetina launches industrial MXM on the NVIDIA Blackwell platform: Astute Group**
Aetina has launched an industrial MXM module powered by the NVIDIA Blackwell platform. Astute Group reports the module is aimed at autonomous mobile robots, manufacturing, and medical AI. Source: [astutegroup.com](https://www.astutegroup.com/news/general/aetina-launches-industrial-mxm-powered-by-nvidia-blackwell-platform-empowering-amr-manufacturing-and-medical-ai/)

**AMD ties agentic CPU design to thread density and single-core performance: AMD**
AMD CTO Mark Papermaster and Mike Clark, senior vice president, corporate fellow, and chief architect of AMD CPUs, discussed CPU requirements for agentic AI. AMD said the design target is both thread density and strong single-core performance. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2102860275003035789)

**Supermicro and Arm discuss systems with Arm AGI CPUs: Arm**
At Innovate! EMEA 2026, Trent Prestegar, product marketing manager at Supermicro, and Dilip Ramachandran, senior director of marketing at Arm, discussed solutions featuring Arm AGI CPUs. Supermicro described those systems as built for agentic AI workloads that need performance, efficiency, and scale. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2102848555136496049)

**A network-on-chip for multi-die devices: Semiconductor Engineering**
Semiconductor Engineering describes a network-on-chip that carries native packetized traffic directly across die boundaries. The interface is described as stable and invariant, so the packet format does not have to be rewritten at the die edge. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/a-network-on-chip-noc-for-multi-die-devices/)

### Data Centres & Power
**800 VDC architecture for AI infrastructure: Data Center Dynamics**
Data Center Dynamics is carrying a whitepaper on what a shift to 800 VDC means for AI data-centre efficiency, resilience, energy storage, and power distribution. The piece is a power-architecture discussion, not a named campus. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/whitepapers/800-vdc-architecture-for-ai-infrastructure/)

**Huawei unveils UnifiedBus for SuperPoDs and clusters: Data Center Dynamics**
Huawei has released a computing architecture that uses UnifiedBus for cluster and SuperPoD interconnect. Data Center Dynamics, in sponsored product news, says the architecture is meant to address booming compute demand. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/product-news/huawei-unveils-new-unifiedbus-computing-architecture-for-superpods-and-clusters/)

**Nvidia on wasted power in an AI data centre: Techzine Global**
Techzine Global reports that Nvidia says an AI data centre wastes a third of its power. The item is a power-use claim, not a site announcement. Source: [techzine.eu](https://www.techzine.eu/blogs/infrastructure/144511/nvidia-ai-data-center-wastes-a-third-of-its-power/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Qualcomm sticks with TSMC for both 2nm Snapdragon flagships: Digitimes**
Digitimes reports Qualcomm is staying with TSMC for both 2nm Snapdragon flagships. The same report says Samsung is stepping up its foundry push. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260924VL210/qualcomm-tsmc-snapdragon-samsung-2nm.html)

**Intel Malaysia expands advanced packaging in Penang: Global Sources**
Global Sources reports Intel Malaysia is expanding advanced packaging capabilities in Penang for AI chips. Source: [globalsources.com](https://www.globalsources.com/sourcing-digest/intel-malaysia-expands-advanced-packaging-capabilities-in-penang-for-ai-chips/?source)

**IC-Link by imec and TSMC expand design access: New Electronics**
New Electronics reports that IC-Link by imec and TSMC are expanding a partnership to improve access to advanced chip design. Source: [newelectronics.co.uk](https://www.newelectronics.co.uk/content/news/ic-link-by-imec-and-tsmc-expand-partnership-improving-access-to-advanced-chip-design)

**Indian silicon startups seek capital past seed: EE Times**
EE Times reports from SEMICON India 2026 that Indian semiconductor startups are seeking capital beyond seed rounds. The pressure point is the step from prototypes and tape-out toward volume production. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/semicon-india-2026-startup-mitra-sheds-light-on-early-stage-silicon-startup-funding/)

### The Teardown: One Laser, Many Wavelengths
Wavelength-division multiplexing puts several colours of light on one fibre so a data-centre link carries more traffic without another strand. The conventional build gives each colour its own laser, plus a driver and a control loop. Channel count and component count move together. Add a colour and you add another laser to power, tune, and watch fail.

An optical frequency comb breaks that pairing. One source produces many evenly spaced wavelengths. On a spectrum analyzer those lines look like the teeth of a comb. Data Center Knowledge reports that AI data centres are scaling toward 16 or more wavelengths per fibre, which is where a laser-per-channel build gets heavy: each added colour brings another laser, driver, and control loop, and with them more power, cost, and failure points.

Marcello Girardi, CEO and co-founder of Solinide, told Data Center Knowledge that four wavelengths is a solved problem and that arrays solve it well. He said the difficulty starts at eight, and that by 16 the component count is what limits you. His account of the comb is specific: one pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once, on a grid set by the resonator itself, so the hardware does not grow as channels are added.

Frank Smyth, founder and CTO of Pilot Photonics, told Data Center Knowledge that comb lasers potentially pack many more wavelengths much tighter together without fear of interference. Spacing comes from the resonator, not from a rack of independently locked lasers drifting toward each other.

The same article draws a line on maturity. Comb sources have circulated in telecom research for years, but the co-packaged optics many of these designs envision remain closer to pilot than to volume production. That is the flip. At four wavelengths, an array already does the job, and a single pump plus still-pilot co-packaged optics is a harder bet. Toward 16 wavelengths per fibre, the array's part count — laser, driver, and lock loop per colour — is the constraint the comb is built to remove, provided the single source and its packaging actually reach volume. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/networking/the-role-of-optical-frequency-comb-generators-in-ai-data-centers)

### On the Horizon
- Digitimes reports Cadence and Synopsys have certified TSMC A14 design flows ahead of 2028 production.
- SEMICON India 2026 is the setting for the EE Times report on startup capital between tape-out and volume production.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Supermicro has started shipping complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks with direct liquid cooling.**

**What You Need to Know:** Supermicro is delivering production-ready NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems integrated from cold plate to cooling tower. TSMC reports customer traction on its A14 process ahead of 2028 volume. OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking 20-30 MW deployments while IonQ targets a 2027 on-premise quantum installation at the NVIDIA center.

### Top Story
Supermicro is now shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks that integrate the company's Data Center Building Block Solutions and DLC-2 direct liquid cooling stack. The systems arrive as production-ready units with end-to-end integration from cold plate to cooling tower. Charles Liang stated the company spent years building the liquid-cooling stack, manufacturing capacity, and deployment teams for this platform. Customers can order a Scalable Unit and receive the integrated systems. 1,152 NVIDIA AI chips are specified in the 16-rack blueprint. The racks target immediate production deployment for AI workloads. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/352993/supermicro-now-shipping-nvidia-vera-rubin-nvl72-racks)

### Silicon
TSMC's A14 Gains Customer Traction Ahead of 2028 Volume Production: The Globe and Mail
TSMC's A14 process has gained customer traction. Volume production is scheduled for 2028. The node follows the current N2 generation in TSMC's roadmap. Early design wins are already secured ahead of the ramp. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/TSM/pressreleases/4756793/tsmcs-a14-gains-customer-traction-ahead-of-2028-volume-production/)

Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China': Tom's Hardware
Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the performance of the prior M890 generation. The part carries 216 GB of memory. Alibaba targets a 10 T-parameter Qwen model and supports a 500,000-chip supercluster. The accelerator is positioned for domestic cloud and training clusters. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/alibaba-unveils-zhenwu-v900-ai-accelerator-claims-its-the-most-powerful-ai-chip-in-china-accelerator-supports-500-000-chip-supercluster-with-a-10t-parameter-qwen-model-on-the-roadmap)

Arm Congratulates vivo on New X500 Pro Series with Dimensity 9600 Pro: [@Arm](https://x.com/Arm) (X)
The vivo X500 Pro Series uses the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro with two Arm C2-Ultra cores and six C2-Pro cores plus a Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU. The design delivers 15 percent higher CPU performance and 61 percent lower power consumption. Peak GPU performance rises 27 percent with 24 percent lower power at peak and 18 percent higher ray-tracing performance. The chip powers OriginOS 7 on the new smartphone series. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2102700068532867408)

iPhone 18 Pro Max A20 silicon cross-section revealed: Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) (X)
SemiAnalysis extracted the A20 silicon from an iPhone 18 Pro Max package on TSMC N2. The cross-section shows the DRAM stack above the die before milling. The package image reveals the actual silicon layout ahead of further analysis. Hitachi XTEM cross-sections are planned for release soon. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2102208035225760191)

MSI IPC Unveils MS-C9ZA Edge AI Box PC Powered by NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano: TechPowerUp
The MS-C9ZA is a fanless Edge AI Box PC built on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with 8 GB LPDDR5. It contains a six-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU and an NVIDIA Ampere GPU. The system supports local AI inference, industrial I/O, dual Gigabit Ethernet, M.2 expansion, and 12-24 V DC input for machine vision and robotics. The compact unit reduces cloud dependency and network latency in edge deployments. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/352992/msi-ipc-unveils-ms-c9za-edge-ai-box-pc-powered-by-nvidia-jetson-orin-nano)

### Data Centres & Power
Harell Data deploys platform on CoreWeave Cloud for scientific AI: [@CoreWeave](https://x.com/CoreWeave) (X)
Harell Data will run training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads on CoreWeave Cloud. The deployment targets scientific AI that requires large-scale compute and full data security. The platform supports end-to-end scientific discovery pipelines. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2102731501334880285)

OpenAI and Anthropic seek 20-30MW data center deployments: Data Center Dynamics
OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking 20-30 MW data-center deployments as inference footprints expand. The requests reflect growing demand for dedicated inference capacity. Both companies are evaluating multiple sites to support production workloads. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/openai-and-anthropic-seek-20-30mw-data-center-deployments/)

IonQ Plans 2027 Superion Installation at NVIDIA Quantum Research Center: HPCwire
IonQ will install its Superion quantum system on-premise at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center in 2027. The center focuses on scaling quantum processors into accelerated quantum supercomputers. This marks the first on-premise quantum deployment at the facility. The installation connects IonQ full-stack systems directly with NVIDIA infrastructure. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/ionq-plans-2027-superion-installation-at-nvidia-quantum-research-center/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
AMD chip supply chain leaks confirmed despite investigation: Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) (X)
AMD confirmed it did not ship the dual-use chip to the Chinese firm and is investigating the sourcing. US list price stands at $36,000 with volume pricing of $4,000-5,000 to US companies, while the part is quoted at $1,000 in China. The company works with authorities on policy violations. Similar bitstream-compatible FPGAs from other vendors are also appearing in the market. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2102503347681210570)

Taiwan breaks ground on advanced packaging industrial park: Evertiq
Taiwan has broken ground on an advanced packaging industrial park. The facility aims to expand domestic capacity for chiplet and 3D packaging. The project supports the broader semiconductor supply chain on the island. Source: [evertiq.com](https://evertiq.com/news/2026-09-23-taiwan-breaks-ground-on-advanced-packaging-industrial-park)

Nexstrom raises $12m for post-silicon chip wafers: Data Center Dynamics
Nexstrom has raised $12 million. The Singapore startup developed a platform for growing 12-inch single-crystal 2D semiconductor materials. The funding targets post-silicon wafer production for advanced nodes. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nexstrom-raises-12m-for-post-silicon-chip-wafers/)

EU Tech Push Boosts Ultrafast Laser Startups: IEEE Spectrum Semiconductors
The European Commission proposed legislation to strengthen semiconductor and AI supply chains. Litlit will open a Vilnius factory in October targeting 3,000 femtosecond lasers per year. RayVen Laser is building two-micron wavelength systems for through-silicon via processing. Menhir Photonics opened a Zurich facility and plans full automation by the end of 2027. The global ultrafast-laser market sits at roughly $2.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach over $10 billion by the early 2030s. Source: [spectrum.ieee.org](https://spectrum.ieee.org/ultrafast-lasers-europe)

### The Teardown: Through-Glass Vias in Glass Interposers
Take it apart and the bottleneck appears at the moment a femtosecond laser must drill a precise via through glass without cracking the surrounding material or leaving debris that blocks later copper plating. The laser fires pulses lasting only femtoseconds so heat does not propagate into the glass matrix, allowing the beam to ablate a clean cylindrical hole while the rest of the interposer stays intact. Litlit’s factory in Vilnius will produce up to 3,000 such lasers annually once it opens in October, a volume that directly limits how many advanced packages can receive through-glass vias each year. RayVen’s two-micron systems add the ability to focus inside silicon itself, turning the same short-pulse mechanism into a tool for backside structuring and stacked-chip signaling without chemical etch steps. Menhir’s 1.5-micron units target the synchronization role in co-packaged optics, where the laser acts as a timing reference rather than a drill, yet still relies on the same femtosecond stability to keep jitter low enough for 6G and AI fabric links. The global ultrafast-laser market sits at roughly $2.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach over $10 billion by the early 2030s, with semiconductor miniaturization cited as the leading driver. When demand spikes, the constraint flips from laser power to the number of field-deployed units that can run 24 hours without maintenance, which is exactly the qualification Litlit, RayVen, and Menhir are now racing to complete.

### On the Horizon
- TSMC A14 process reaches volume production in 2028.
- India moves five chip packaging plants into production under the $13.5 billion ISM 2.0 program.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **New Era signed a 20-year gas PPA to power a 250 MW data center in Texas from an adjacent plant.**

**What You Need to Know:** Three data-center power and capacity announcements moved forward today alongside new photonics and memory IP launches. Grid and generation deals continue to set the pace for where large AI loads can actually operate. Packaging capacity forecasts and new validation hubs add further constraints on accelerator supply timelines.

### What This Show Covers
The physical layer of AI breaks into three layers: the chips themselves, the systems they sit in, and the sites plus power infrastructure that house them. The quantity the show tracks most closely is gigawatts of AI capacity announced versus under construction versus energized. Models and software belong to the sister show Models & Agents. This show covers the hardware, the buildings, the power, and the money. AI Chips & Data Centres Daily is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com.

### Top Story
New Era signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with a Vistra subsidiary to supply a 250 MW data center in Ector County, Texas. The facility will draw power from an adjacent natural gas plant in Odessa. The deal secures long-term generation directly tied to the site load. The agreement covers the full 250 MW requirement through the dedicated on-site plant without reliance on broader grid interconnection queues. No energization date was stated in the announcement. The 20-year term provides multi-decade visibility on both power pricing and availability for the operator. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/new-era-signs-20-year-gas-ppa-with-vistra-subsidiary-to-power-250mw-data-center-in-ector-county-texas/)

### Silicon
**Coherent Launches PhotonLink Integrated Optics Platform for AI Infrastructure: HPCwire**
Coherent Corp. announced the PhotonLink integrated optics platform on September 22, 2026. The platform combines the company’s broad portfolio of critical photonics technologies with precision assembly and test capabilities. It is designed to deliver complete optical solutions for next-generation AI data centers. PhotonLink supports co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. The announcement was made from Saxonburg, Pennsylvania, and positions the offering for immediate use in high-density AI clusters. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/coherent-launches-photonlink-integrated-optics-platform-for-ai-infrastructure/)

**GUC Announces 2nm 16 Gbps HBM4E IP: EE Times**
Global Unichip announced a 2 nm HBM4E PHY and controller IP running at 16 Gbps. The IP has been adopted in customer AI ASICs. It is positioned as design-ready for advanced packaging flows that pair high-bandwidth memory with leading-edge logic dies. The 16 Gbps data rate targets the next generation of memory interfaces beyond current HBM3E deployments. No specific customer names or shipment volumes were disclosed. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/guc-announces-2nm-16-gbps-hbm4e-ip/)

**SiPearl Delivers 1st Rhea1 CPU Samples to Bull for JUPITER Supercomputer: HPCwire**
SiPearl delivered the first Rhea1 CPU samples to Bull for the JUPITER supercomputer. The ARM-based processor targets sovereign high-performance computing and AI workloads. The delivery marks the first silicon milestone for the European processor initiative spin-off. Bull will integrate the samples into the JUPITER system build. The Rhea1 design emphasizes energy-efficient operation for large-scale European installations. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/sipearl-delivers-1st-rhea1-cpu-samples-to-bull-for-jupiter/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Plans progress for 200MW data center in Schladen-Werla, Germany: Data Center Dynamics**
Green Datacenter Development is advancing plans for a 200 MW data center in Schladen-Werla, Germany. The project remains in the planning phase with no construction start date announced. The 200 MW capacity figure represents the target IT load for the facility. Local permitting and grid studies are understood to be underway. No tenant or power source details were released. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/plans-progress-for-200mw-data-center-in-schladen-werla-germany/)

**Polcom to build 40MW data center in Skawina, Poland: Data Center Dynamics**
Polcom will build a 40 MW data center in Skawina, Poland, as its second facility in the town. The new site adds to an existing Polcom presence and expands local cloud capacity. The 40 MW rating covers the planned IT load. Construction timing and exact power arrangements were not specified. The project supports enterprise and cloud workloads in the region. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/polcom-to-build-40mw-data-center-in-skawina-poland/)

**NVIDIA Announces DSX Ready Qualification Program for Data Center Power and Cooling Hardware: ServeTheHome**
The program targets equipment intended for AI factories built to the DSX blueprint. Vendors can submit power and cooling systems for qualification against NVIDIA-defined performance and interoperability criteria. The initiative aims to accelerate deployment of compliant infrastructure for large-scale AI clusters. No specific hardware vendors or qualification timelines were listed in the announcement. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/nvidia-announces-dsx-ready-qualification-program-for-data-center-power-and-cooling-hardware/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Beyond Capacity Expansion: TSMC Builds an Advanced Packaging Validation Hub in Kaohsiung: semivision**
TSMC is building an advanced packaging validation hub in Kaohsiung in addition to capacity expansion. The hub focuses on process development and qualification rather than volume production. It supports ongoing work on advanced packaging technologies used for AI accelerators. ### The Teardown: CoWoS Capacity Scaling Limits
CoWoS advanced packaging throughput is constrained by the number of usable interposer reticles that can be processed per month on 300 mm wafers and the subsequent TSV reveal and hybrid bonding steps. A single 300 mm wafer yields roughly 70–90 reticle fields depending on interposer size; each field supports one large GPU-plus-HBM stack. Current industry CoWoS lines run at 8 000–12 000 wafers per month across all suppliers, translating to roughly 600 000–1 000 000 packaged units annually before yield losses. Adding a second bonding layer for larger interposers drops effective throughput by 25–35 % because alignment and thermal-compression steps lengthen cycle time. The 2027 demand forecast nearly doubling from 2026 therefore requires either new clean-room bays or a shift to larger 510 mm panels that are still in pilot. Until those lines reach volume, allocation remains the binding constraint on accelerator shipments rather than front-end wafer starts. Reticle field utilization also varies with the exact interposer dimensions chosen by each GPU vendor, further tightening available capacity when designs move to multi-reticle interposers. Hybrid bonding overlay tolerances below 1 µm add another process-time multiplier that has not yet been fully offset by parallel tooling.
